On the topic of the event, I did get in the solo game to finish the core set cycle of environments, but my wife & I did some Christmas gift planning for family members, so I didn't get to Silver Gulch.

Legacy, Unity, and Haka took on Ambuscade in Insula Primalis, and started out with a rough go of it. Ambuscade pulled a Vanish on his first turn, and Haka deemed it necessary to wipe the starting Sonic Mine in order to keep it from becoming dino chow, but then promptly became a T-Rex snack himself. I became convinced of the utility of Flash Forge through being able to use it (after skipping Unity's play & power phases on her first turn due to lack of a way to get bots into play) to find a Construction Pylon, Workbench, and Swift Bot, which then collectively fueled getting two Platform Bots, a Champion Bot, and pair of Raptor Bots (the latter in succession) out. The first Raptor Bot didn't survive a full round thanks to getting pummeled by Ambuscade, but his successor helped make a big difference. Once Ambuscade came out of hiding, Unity's bots and Haka just tore him apart.

posts.name: Envisioner
posts.cooked:
jffdougan:

Ambuscade pulled a Vanish … once Ambuscade came out of hiding, Unity's bots and Haka just tore him apart.

That's usually how it works.  Makes him a very annoying and silly villain, usually an utter putz, but immensely frustrating on occasions.  It's weird, he has Vanish and Traps that want him to play a slow waiting game, and he has all those "shuffle and play a card" tricks that make him super-fast, so on balance he's neither fast nor slow, just schizophrenic.  Probably no other villain so badly wishes he could stack his own deck instead of having to be random…and yet, he's even more random than most villains because he keeps shuffling.  (This is probably based on the same logic that gave Expatriette the "Play a card" power, which every single other hero wants more than she does.)
